subject: Urgent: headroom starvation & token-queue bleed impacting EmergeBank (reserved throughput)
messages:
From: Simon Clarke <simon.clarke@emergebank.com>
To: ops@emergebank.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: High latency and 5xx spike from reserved pool since 06:00 PT

Team —

We started seeing sustained 99th-percentile latencies jump to ~2.8s and a rising rate of 5xx for our production routes (payment-reconciliation) starting ~06:00 PT. Throughput is also throttled despite our reserved quota. This is hitting our session timeouts and causing retries in our stack.

Attached a small perf snapshot from our side (perf_snapshot_20260227.log). Can you confirm whether this is an internal saturation on the dedicated GPU pool or a routing fallback to a lower-tier model? EmergeBank is seeing a measurable user-impact (5–7% failed jobs) — we need ETA and whether this will breach SLA.

We are on a monthly reserved contract (DL-78923). Please escalate as needed.

— Simon
Simon Clarke
Head of Platform Ops, EmergeBank

Forwarding Simon's alert — this looks like the reserved-capacity pool for us-west-2 has reduced headroom and we're seeing token-queue growth on low-latency hotpaths. Initial ask:

1) Mina — please confirm whether the dedicated pool in us-west-2 is at capacity or whether there was a kernel/driver regression pushed in the 05:00 deploy window. Include GPU utilization, NVLink stats, and per-instance qdepth.
2) Naomi — pull the routing logs for EmergeBank's model variant and confirm any automatic fallback to quantized variants. If fallback occurred, include percent of requests routed and timestamps.
3) Marissa — loop in Sales/CS and ask Simon for a short list of failing endpoints and their business impact; request permission to open an incident bridge and inform them we'll provide an executive readout within 3 hours.

This must be treated as P1 for the customer and flagged for leadership visibility if we confirm reserved throughput shortfall.

— Karthik
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ops@emergebank.com
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High latency and 5xx spike from reserved pool since 06:00 PT

Karthik / team — quick diagnostics below:

- Summary: Dedicated pool for us-west-2 shows high GPU util (avg 94%), sustained queue depth on token cache hotshards, and 3 machines reporting elevated kernel preemption leading to slow token-dequeue. No recent kernel version pushed after 02:30; however, a scheduler tuning change rolled at 04:45 (auto-batcher tweak) that increased batch coalescing on priority queues.
- Impact window: 06:00 — present; tail latency and 5xx correlate with specific hotshards (nodes: gpu-uw2-32, gpu-uw2-33, gpu-uw2-47).
- Immediate mitigation applied (11:00): reduced batch_coalesce_factor on priority route, drained hotshard gpu-uw2-47 and shifted 18% of EmergeBank traffic to warm pool (temporary). That reduced 99p latency from 2.8s -> 1.6s but 5xx rate still ~1.1% (baseline 0.05%).
- Next steps (in-progress): reprovision +2 GPUs to the reserved pool (takes ~45m for node boot + warm-up), enable KV-prefix caching for high-hit routes (safe toggle), and a rolling remediation to back out the 04:45 tuning if results don't improve.

Attaching short queue dump snapshot: sla_queue_summary_q1.pdf (see highlighted hotshard queue pileup).

I recommend we open an incident bridge and prepare an executive note for the CTO/CSO with the customer impact, timeline, and a credit remediation proposal if SLA is violated.

— Mina
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

[attachment: sla_queue_summary_q1.pdf (application/pdf, 220KB)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Urgent: headroom starvation & token-queue bleed impacting EmergeBank (reserved throughput)

Team / Simon — brief exec-ready summary and asks:

- Current state: mitigation reduced tail lat from 2.8s to ~1.3s on most routes. 5xx rate dropped from 1.6% to 0.6% after shifting traffic and batch_coalesce rollback. However a small subset of reconciliation endpoints still see elevated retries.
- Root cause hypothesis: scheduler tuning + uneven hotshard placement caused headroom starvation on a subset of reserved nodes; auto-fallback routing increased load on adjacent nodes and amplified token-queueing.
- Immediate actions taken: +2 GPUs provisioned into reserved pool (complete at 16:15 PT), KV-prefix cache enabled for high-hit keys, and a temporary route-level rate cap for the heaviest reconciliation endpoint (reduces QPS by ~12%).
- Customer ask: Simon, can your team validate if the temporary rate cap is acceptable for the next 2 hours while we validate warm pool behavior? We'll share a rollback plan if it causes any processing backlog on your side.
- Executive ask: Marissa — please draft a one-page exec readout for EmergeBank covering: timeline, impact, mitigation, credits if SLA breach confirmed, and a 30/60/90 day remediation plan (hotshard placement hardening, scheduler gating, reserved headroom thresholds). I will copy to leadership for approval.

I'll keep bridge open until we confirm sustained <0.1% 5xx and 99p <600ms for EmergeBank routes.

— Karthik
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
